title: Equivalent forms of weak contractibility
statement:
Let $W$ be an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with representable sheaf
$h_W=\Hom_X(-,W)$ ([det-pe-topos-functoriality-site]). The following are equivalent:

1. every epimorphism of sheaves of sets $F\to h_W$ has a section;
2. $h_W$ is projective in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}})$: for every epimorphism $F\to G$ and every
   map $h_W\to G$ there is a lift $h_W\to F$;
3. for every epimorphism of sheaves $F\to G$ the map $F(W)\to G(W)$ is surjective.

An object satisfying these conditions is called *weakly contractible*. Every affine
$W=\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $D$ w-contractible is weakly contractible
([det-pe-wcb-projective]).

proof.text: By [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site](2), $h_W$ is a sheaf. Sheaves form a full subcategory of presheaves by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Applying [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] to the underlying presheaves gives $\operatorname{Hom}(h_W,F)\cong F(W)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(h_W,G)\cong G(W)$. For $\alpha:F\to G$ and $s:h_W\to F$, naturality in the presheaf gives $\operatorname{Yoneda}(\alpha\circ s)=\alpha_W(\operatorname{Yoneda}(s))$. Thus for each $y:h_W\to G$, the equation $\alpha\circ s=y$ is equivalent to $\alpha_W(\operatorname{Yoneda}(s))=\operatorname{Yoneda}(y)$, proving $2\Leftrightarrow3$.

source.place: First paragraph, 2 iff 3; Stacks categories.tex Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda

proof.text: Assume condition 1. Given an epimorphism $\alpha:F\to G$ and $y:h_W\to G$, define $P(V)=\{(a,t)\in F(V)\times h_W(V):\alpha_V(a)=y_V(t)\}$, with coordinatewise restrictions. Naturality preserves the defining equality. For a matching family in $P$, glue its two coordinates uniquely in the sheaves $F$ and $h_W$ using [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; the two resulting sections of $G$ agree locally and hence agree by separatedness. Therefore the glued pair lies in $P$, uniquely, so $P$ is a sheaf. Its coordinate projections are sheaf morphisms; any pair of morphisms to $F$ and $h_W$ with equal composites to $G$ factors uniquely by pairing the components. Thus $P$ is the pullback $F\times_Gh_W$.

source.place: Second paragraph, 1 implies 2: explicit construction of the pullback sheaf

proof.text: For $t\in h_W(V)$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] to $\alpha$ and $y_V(t)\in G(V)$. On some covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ there are $a_i\in F(V_i)$ with $\alpha(a_i)=y_V(t)|_{V_i}=y_{V_i}(t|_{V_i})$. Thus $(a_i,t|_{V_i})\in P(V_i)$ lifts $t|_{V_i}$. The converse direction of the same criterion shows that the projection $p:P\to h_W$ is an epimorphism. This proves exactly the pullback stability needed in the blueprint without invoking a further topos theorem.

source.place: Second paragraph, 1 implies 2: pullback projection epimorphic; Stacks sites.tex Tags 00WM and 00WN, definition-sheaves-injective-surjective and lemma-mono-epi-sheaves

proof.text: By condition 1 the epimorphism $p$ constructed in steps 2–3 has a section $r:h_W\to P$. Let $q:P\to F$ be the other projection. Then $\alpha\circ q\circ r=y\circ p\circ r=y$, so $q\circ r$ is the required lift. This proves $1\Rightarrow2$. Conversely, condition 2 applied to an epimorphism $F\to h_W$ and $\mathrm{id}_{h_W}$ supplies a section, proving $2\Rightarrow1$.

source.place: Second and third paragraphs: composing the section with the projection, and lifting the identity

proof.text: For an affine object $W=\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $D$ w-contractible, clause 1 of [det-pe-wcb-projective] says exactly that every epimorphism $F\to h_W$ has a section. Thus condition 1 holds and the equivalences proved above give all three conditions. This proves the final assertion and agrees with the weak-contractibility terminology in the statement.

source.place: Final sentence: w-contractible affines satisfy condition 1

proof_origin.place: All three equivalence paragraphs and final assertion, expanded by the local-surjectivity criterion of Stacks Tag 00WN
